sentences.text: Erromenosteus was an extinct, medium-sized arthrodire placoderm belonging to the family Brachythoracidae. These animals possessed bullet-shaped heads and curved jaws adapted for crushing food.

The holotype for Erromenosteus lucifer is a skull measuring 12 cm in length. The species Erromenosteus brachyrostris is known from a single holotype skull that is 6 cm long. Erromenosteus concavus is known from multiple specimens with skull lengths averaging between 7 cm and 13 cm. The holotype skull of Erromenosteus inflatus measures 8 cm in length. The holotype skull of Erromenosteus diensti is 12 cm long, though it was originally classified in the genus Paraleiosteus due to differences in its scapulo-coracoid bone.
The genus Erromenosteus was first described by Jaekel in 1919, with the type species being Erromenosteus lucifer.
Erromenosteus has been synonymized with the genera Leiosteus, Paraleiosteus, Coccosteus, and Brachydeirus. Modern classification places it as a basal member of the superfamily Dinichthyloidea.
Erromenosteus lived during the Frasnian stage, between 382.31 and 372.15 million years ago. Fossils are found in the Late Frasnian Kellwasserkalk facies in Bad Wildungen and Bicken, Germany.
The name Erromenosteus koeneni is apparently a nomen nudum, meaning it was never properly described despite a holotype skull measuring 60 mm in length.
